title: Allow direct controls during workbench host jobs
platforms: Windows GNU build; Wine/Xvfb synthetic interpreter
changes: Allow direct menu Start to use the shared action handler while a separate workbench host worker remains active. Preserve the worker busy indicator and cancellation; profile and host-tool starts and background validation remain serialized.
validation: A synthetic long-running host worker reproduced the former menu-only block while CLI inspection succeeded. With the fix, CLI, menu and interactive console produced the same readonly inspection while the host worker stayed tracked; explicit cancellation stopped the worker and guest state remained unchanged. Protected inputs and normal GUI closure verified.

Windows GNU menu/runtime test builds and runtime build passed; Wine passed 7 tool-form, 8 workbench, 34 local-control and 10 command tests. The generated Atlas task reference was synchronized with the checklist.
limitations: The host worker was a synthetic waiting process; this does not establish behavior of every host tool, native Windows, physical input or full DBG2-13 parity.
